children: Flowserve's top finance executive, Amy Schwetz, is leaving the provider of flow-control products and services at the end of the month to take a leadership position at another company.

Flowserve on Monday said Brian Ezzell, currently vice president of financial planning and analysis, treasurer and investor relations, will succeed Schwetz as senior vice president and chief financial officer on Oct. 1.
Schwetz has been Flowserve's chief financial officer since joining the Irving, Texas, company in February 2020.
Ezzell, 44 years old, joined Flowserve in his current post in October 2024.
Flowserve said Ezzell will receive an annual base salary of $625,000 as finance chief, along with an annual bonus with a target of 75% of his base pay.
